rows.title: Alhambra Mk2 Tailgate Gas Strut Failure
rows.howToFix: Manual-strut pair replacement €60-€120 in parts, 15-30 min DIY. Electric tailgate module €350-€600 per side. Use the manual override (button on inside of tailgate) if a strut fails suddenly — don't rely on the remaining one.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Handbrake lever travel increases (parking-brake recall, manual lever cars)
rows.howToFix: Check the VIN with SEAT or the applicable national recall service. For a vehicle included in R/2019/039, the official remedy is to readjust the handbrake assembly and fit a locking device to the nut; the DVSA page says recall work is provided without charge. Do not buy a handbrake cable, caliper or adjuster from this page; recall inclusion and the required repair must be confirmed from the VIN.

rows.title: Rear brake discs corrode and seize at very low mileage
rows.howToFix: Replace corroded rear discs and pads (and seized handbrake cables/calipers where applicable). Mitigate recurrence by performing periodic firm braking to scrub the discs, and where safe parking on level ground without the electronic parking brake. Specify better-quality discs on replacement.

rows.title: Rear left seatbelt buckle can release involuntarily (Takata double-buckle recall)
rows.howToFix: Have the recall (SEAT/DVSA seatbelt campaign) carried out free at a dealer — a plastic spacer is fitted into the rear double-buckle to prevent unintended release. Until fixed, owners were advised not to use the centre-rear seat. Verify completion via VIN recall lookup.

rows.title: 1.5 TSI EVO "kangarooing" / cold-start hesitation and low-speed jerking
rows.howToFix: Apply the VW Group / SEAT engine-control software update (released Feb 2020, per TSB 2470) at a dealer. Disabling auto-hold and stop-start reduces the worst of the low-speed jerk. Persistent cases after the update should be checked for separate mechanical faults (e.g., injectors, coils). Allowing the engine to warm before hard driving minimizes symptoms.

rows.title: 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) jerky shifts and mechatronic failure
rows.howToFix: Diagnose the mechatronic unit; recondition/replace the valve body with the superseded (thicker-wall) design that VW/Audi released to cure the accumulator-plate failure, or fit a remanufactured mechatronic unit. Use only the correct DSG fluid and keep to service intervals (DSG oil/filter change). Have jerky-shift complaints scanned early before clutch-pack damage occurs.

rows.title: Early 1.0 TSI clutch and injector failures (build-quality teething faults)
rows.howToFix: Address under warranty: replace failed injectors or clutch assemblies and verify correct reassembly (the burning-smell case was a missed clip). For wastegate-actuator hesitation, have the actuator/turbo checked. Buyers of used early cars should review service history for prior clutch/injector work.

rows.title: Infotainment system goes black and continuously reboots
rows.howToFix: Apply the latest infotainment software update at a dealer; a hard reset (hold the power/volume button ~10 seconds, or leave the car off overnight) is a temporary workaround. Where software fails to resolve it, the infotainment control unit has been replaced under warranty/goodwill.
rows.dispositionReason: The prescribed remedy is dealer, campaign, recall, or software work.

rows.title: Petrol particulate filter (GPF) blocks on short-journey/city driving
rows.howToFix: When the GPF warning appears, follow the SEAT manual: drive for ~15 minutes at a minimum of 60 km/h (37 mph) in 4th/5th gear to allow regeneration. Owners doing mostly short trips should schedule periodic longer/faster runs. A badly clogged filter may need a forced regeneration or replacement.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Ateca 2.0 TSI Water Pump / Thermostat Failure
rows.howToFix: Complete water pump + thermostat module replacement €400-€700 incl. labor and coolant. Use VW G13 coolant (pink, do not mix with G12++ green-pink) and bleed properly — air locks are common.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: Wheel Arch and Body Seam Corrosion (Mk3/Mk4)
rows.howToFix: Treat early surface rust by cutting back to clean metal, treating and resealing; for established/perforating rust, replace the affected panel or arch section. Apply cavity wax and underbody protection, and keep drainage channels clear. Pursue an anti-corrosion warranty claim where the car still qualifies.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: DSG DQ200 (7-Speed Dry Clutch) Mechatronic Failure
rows.howToFix: Mechatronic replacement (refurbished unit + coding) €900-€1,800; new €2,000-€3,000. Dry clutch pack replacement €1,200-€2,000. Some markets had VW extended-warranty coverage — check records. Avoid riding the brake on inclines (DQ200 hates it).

rows.title: Battery Drain / Parasitic Drain Requiring ECU Software Update
rows.howToFix: Have the parasitic drain measured and apply the SEAT control-module software update at a franchised dealer (the documented fix). Replace the battery only if it has been damaged by repeated deep discharge.
rows.dispositionReason: At least one replacement is conditional on a stated diagnostic result.

rows.title: DQ200 7-Speed Dry-Clutch DSG Mechatronic and Clutch Failure
rows.howToFix: Diagnose with VCDS to distinguish mechatronic versus clutch-pack faults. Failed mechatronic units should be replaced or reconditioned with the superseded uprated valve body; worn dry-clutch packs require replacement. Keep up with the DSG service (oil change where applicable) and ensure the correct, updated fluid spec is used.

diagnosticDispositions.excerpt: Diagnose with VCDS to distinguish mechatronic versus clutch-pack faults.

rows.title: Electric Power Steering (TRW) Loss of Assistance / No Communication
rows.howToFix: Diagnose with VCDS for communication/angle-sensor faults; check power and ground at the pump connector and CAN-bus wiring. Recalibrate/replace the steering-angle sensor if faulty; many cases are resolved only by replacing or reconditioning the TRW power-steering pump/control module.

check power and ground at the pump connector and CAN-bus wiring.

rows.title: 1.6 TDI (EA189) EGR Valve Failure - Aggravated by Dieselgate Emissions Fix
rows.howToFix: Clean or replace the EGR valve/cooler assembly; address related intake carbon build-up. If the failure followed the emissions software update, pursue a goodwill/warranty claim with SEAT/VW. Some owners seek an emissions software rollback (note legal/MOT implications in the EU/UK).

rows.title: Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) Clogging on TDI Diesels
rows.howToFix: Complete a high-speed motorway run to allow a passive/active regeneration to finish; if blocked, perform a forced regeneration via diagnostics or a professional DPF clean, and replace if saturated. Check engine oil for diesel dilution and change oil if contaminated. Avoid repeated short trips and interrupted regen cycles.

rows.title: Ibiza / Leon 1.6 TDI Common-Rail Injector Failure
rows.howToFix: Back-leak test (10 min) confirms diagnosis. Single injector replacement €300-€600 incl. coding. Full set (4) €1,000-€1,800. Use VW 507.00 spec oil and quality diesel from major-brand stations.

rows.title: 1.2 TSI (EA111) Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
rows.howToFix: At the first sign of cold-start rattle, replace the timing chain, tensioner and guides with VW's superseded reinforced kit (and the anti-jump cover). Do not delay - continued driving risks the chain jumping and catastrophic valve/piston damage. Many specialists recommend proactive replacement on pre-2013 engines.

rows.title: Integrated Water Pump / Thermostat Housing Coolant Leak (TSI)
rows.howToFix: Replace the complete water pump/thermostat housing unit (commonly done alongside the timing belt service on belt-driven TSI variants). Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect hoses. Address promptly to avoid overheating damage.

rows.title: Ibiza 1.2 TSI (EA111) Timing Chain Stretch
rows.howToFix: Updated tensioner is a stopgap (~€200-€350 fitted). Full chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides) €700-€1,200. Some independents recommend replacement at 80,000 km regardless of symptoms. Use VW 504.00/507.00 oil at 10,000 km max.

rows.title: Leon Mk2 2.0 TFSI (EA888 Gen 1/2) Oil Consumption
rows.howToFix: Piston/ring replacement is the durable fix (€2,500-€4,500). Check service-history records for VW extended warranty action — eligible cars get the work free. Top-up between services and use 5W-40 VW 502.00 spec (better than 5W-30 for these engines).

rows.title: Leon Mk2 Electric Window Regulator Cable Failure
rows.howToFix: Replacement regulator kit (cables + plastic clips) €40-€80 in parts; €150-€300 incl. labor. DIY is straightforward (door card off, 4 bolts) but takes care to align cable runs. OEM regulators last longer than the cheapest pattern parts.

rows.title: Leon Mk2 2.0 TDI PD (BKD) Injector Failure
rows.howToFix: Single injector replacement €400-€700 incl. coding. Full set (4) €1,400-€2,000. If head crack present, head rebuild adds €1,200-€2,000 more. Use VW 507.00 oil at 10,000 km max, NOT long-life intervals.

rows.title: TDI Dual-Mass Flywheel (DMF) Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the dual-mass flywheel, usually together with the clutch as a job (the labour overlaps). A solid (single-mass) flywheel conversion is a common owner alternative but adds noise/vibration. Avoid labouring the engine at low rpm to extend DMF life.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: Leon Mk2 1.4 TSI Twincharger Timing Chain + Supercharger
rows.howToFix: Chain kit €700-€1,200. Supercharger clutch repair €350-€700 (rebuild) or new pulley €600-€1,000. Many independents recommend ditching the supercharger if budget-limited (remap removes its operation) — power drops but reliability improves.
rows.dispositionReason: No positive owner-buyable repair prescription was found.

rows.title: 1.2/1.4 TSI (EA111) Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
rows.howToFix: Replace the timing chain, tensioner and guides (and oil feed pipe) as a kit at the first sign of cold-start rattle - do not delay, as a skipped chain on this interference engine can destroy the engine. Use updated tensioner part numbers. Many owners pre-emptively replace the tensioner. Keep oil changes short (every ~10k or sooner) as worn/sludged oil accelerates tensioner wear.
rows.dispositionReason: The solution prescribes an owner-buyable component or existing commerce requires re-review.

rows.title: 1.8/2.0 TSI (EA888) Oil Consumption and Intake-Valve Carbon Buildup
rows.howToFix: For oil use: monitor level frequently, fit updated PCV valve, and in severe Gen 2 cases replace pistons/rings. For carbon: walnut-blast the intake valves (typically every ~40k-50k miles) and consider a catch can to cut blow-by. Use the correct VW 504.00 oil and stick to sensible change intervals.

rows.howToFix: Diagnose with VCDS/ODIS. The mechatronic unit is typically replaced or rebuilt (uprated accumulator and valve body). Some failures are covered by VW Group goodwill/extended warranty campaigns. Use only the specified DSG fluid and adhere to fluid-change intervals to prolong life.

rows.title: EA189 TDI Diesel: EGR/DPF Clogging and Post-Dieselgate Oil Dilution

Monitor oil level/dilution and shorten oil-change intervals if doing many short trips. Use correct low-SAPS (e.g. VW 507.00) oil.
